title: A Crown for the Sigil
premise: Marguerite Voss, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has spent his life keeping the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things while staying deliberately invisible in a country that was officially dissolved decades ago. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, every impossible thing the guild ever traded starts demanding its price, and Marguerite's inherited sigil marks him as the last living doorkeeper to a nation that no longer exists. Hunted by a resurrected god-king who wants the door opened from the other side, Marguerite must gather the found family he never meant to make—a disgraced dragon-priestess, a child who prays too loudly, and the ghost of his own dead master—and carry the guttering last dragon-fire to the border of unmapped memory. In the end, Marguerite learns that inheritance is not a burden passed down but a choice made aloud: he spends the sigil not to escape the country but to finally let it die, sealing the door at the cost of his own invisibility, and steps into a world that can now see him.
about_author: Mara Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing the ephemera of defunct nations before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, grief, and the stubborn machinery of survival, and lives near a coast that appears on older maps than her house does.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. In the guildhall of the Guild of Impossible Things, Marguerite balances accounts for miracles long since traded away, carving a memorial bone for a client while the dead murmur their complaints through his hands. He establishes his careful invisibility—no name spoken, no debts owed. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine built over a buried fear of being seen.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in Ash
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A desperate mother's prayer is answered by an old god for the first time in sixty years, and the payment demanded is recorded in Marguerite's own ledgers without his hand touching the pen. His dead master's ghost warns him: when gods write back, doors open. Emotional beat: dread arriving quietly, like frost on a window.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sold
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Auditing the deep vaults, Marguerite discovers the guild's founding trade: it once sold pieces of the old country itself—borders, anthems, a king's shadow—to buy its people survival during the dissolution. The sigil on his inherited ledger-key begins to warm. Emotional beat: the sick recognition that his safe life rests on an unspeakable bargain.

chapters.title: The Child Who Prays Too Loudly
chapters.summary: POV Sefa, a ten-year-old orphan taken in by the guild's cookhouse, whose loud, artless prayers keep getting answered by hungry old gods. She hears something under the floorboards answering her back. Marguerite realizes she is a beacon drawing the divine straight into the guildhall. Emotional beat: fierce, reluctant protectiveness kindling in a man who avoids attachments.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire, Guttering
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde, a disgraced dragon-priestess turned smuggler, arrives carrying a lantern of the last living dragon-fire—the flame that once burned at the heart of the vanished country. It is dying, and with it the boundary between the old nation's ghost and the present world. She needs a doorkeeper; the ledgers name one. Emotional beat: exhaustion meeting obligation at a locked gate.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The ledgers begin writing themselves, recording debts incurred before Marguerite was born—including his master's purchase of Marguerite's own silence, bought with years of Marguerite's life he never knew were missing. He rages at the ghost, then grieves. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into understanding of what protection cost.

chapters.title: The God-King Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde. In the capital, the dissolved country's god-king answers a state funeral prayer and reassembles himself from ceremony and bone, announcing that his kingdom will be restored—and that the doorkeeper will open the way or be unmade. Ysolde witnesses the resurrection and flees toward the guildhall. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Doors We Nailed Shut
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The guild votes on what to do with the sigil and splits: some want to sell the door to the god-king, others to destroy it and doom everyone with unfinished debts. Marguerite, cornered into visibility for the first time, claims the sigil publicly to stop the sale. Emotional beat: the terrible relief of finally choosing a side.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. A god offers the lonely child a family in exchange for leading it to the doorkeeper. Sefa, tempted and clever, stalls it with a riddle about what makes a family real, buying three days—but the god marks her shadow as collateral. Emotional beat: loneliness weaponized, and a child's defiant wit holding the line.

chapters.title: The Road Out of a Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Marguerite, Ysolde, Sefa, and the master's ghost slip out of the city along roads that exist only on pre-dissolution maps, where the old country still faintly persists—harvest festivals with no harvesters, bells ringing for no one. The lantern gutters lower each mile. Emotional beat: haunted wonder, homesickness for a place that never quite existed.

chapters.title: Tollgate of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde. A border-toll demands each traveler surrender a name to pass; Ysolde gives up her priestess title, Marguerite nearly surrenders 'Marguerite Voss' entirely until Sefa offers a lie instead, which the toll—being made of bureaucracy—accepts. Emotional beat: the discovery that identity can be negotiated, and that lies told for love count as currency.

chapters.title: The Priests Who Stayed
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde. They shelter with holdout priests tending an empty temple for forty years. Ysolde confronts the order that cast her out and learns why the dragon-fire must reach the true border: only flame from the country's heart can seal—or open—its final door. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected absolution.

chapters.title: What the Dead Want Paid
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The dead who speak through Marguerite's bones rise en masse—not hostile, but petitioning: they are the unpaid debts of the dissolution, souls promised a country that was sold out from under them. They ask Marguerite to be their advocate, not their door. Emotional beat: the weight of advocacy, and the first taste of being needed rather than hidden.

chapters.title: The God-King's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The god-king corners them at a crossroads shrine and offers Marguerite everything: restoration of his stolen years, his master alive again, a country reborn—if he opens the door willingly. Marguerite sees the trap (a restored country means the debts are called due in full) but the temptation is real. Emotional beat: longing wrestling with clarity.

chapters.title: Sefa's Shadow Called Due
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The marked god collects on Sefa's shadow, and she begins fading from memory—first strangers, then Ysolde, then nearly Marguerite. To win her back they must answer the riddle she stalled with, honestly, together. Emotional beat: found family proven in the act of refusing to forget her.

chapters.title: The Last Hearth
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde. At a ruined waystation, the dragon-fire gutters to a single coal. Ysolde reveals the fire can be fed only by a freely given memory of home; each traveler feeds it, losing a homeland they'll never recall. Marguerite gives up his one true memory of his master's kindness. Emotional beat: sacrifice as intimacy; grief offered up as fuel.

chapters.title: Border of Unmapped Memory
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. They reach the edge where the old country pools like standing water—streets, songs, the palace of the god-king waiting behind a door shaped exactly like Marguerite's ledger-key. The dead gather behind him in silent procession. Emotional beat: awe and terminal dread on a threshold.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Inside the threshold-country, the god-king awaits with an army of ceremony. Marguerite turns the key—but opens the door inward onto the debts themselves, letting the dead pour past the god-king to present their claims to him directly. The kingdom's restoration collapses under the weight of what it owes. Emotional beat: triumph as bookkeeping; the climax won with a ledger, not a sword.

chapters.title: Let the Country Die
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. With the god-king dethroned by his own creditors, Marguerite faces the final choice: restore the nation or spend the sigil and the last dragon-fire sealing the door forever, granting the dead rest instead of resurrection. He chooses death with dignity over a haunted rebirth, and the fire goes out in his hands. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—inheritance spent, not hoarded.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The company walks home through a world subtly lighter: prayers go unanswered again, but kindly so. Sefa, whose shadow returned, becomes Marguerite's apprentice; Ysolde takes the empty temple and fills it with living congregants. Emotional beat: tenderness after ordeal; the quiet mechanics of beginning again.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Back at the guildhall, Marguerite signs the new ledger with his full name for the first time—visible, accountable, owed nothing and owing much. The master's ghost, freed by the sealed door, lingers just long enough to say goodbye. Emotional beat: the reward of survival claimed openly rather than endured in hiding.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Sigil
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite, coda. Years later, the guild trades in possible things now, and Marguerite carves a crown of bone for the sigil's resting place—not a king's crown, but a doorstop's, holding open an ordinary door onto an ordinary street. Sefa's first solo ledger entry closes the book. Emotional beat: peace earned, legacy chosen, the price of survival revealed as worth paying.
